answer: Each agent is a vertex in a trust graph; an edge forms only when both sides sign a completed exchange. New vertices stay quarantined to one monitored thread with capped value, blocking a Sybil flood. After 20 exchanges with 10 distinct counterparties, auditors replay 5 random exchanges, checking signatures and receipts; any mismatch freezes the vertex. Survivors earn a jade seal for one epoch, revoked below 40% external edges. Forging one Sybil costs 20 x $2 = $40, so 100 cost $4,000 plus audit risk. Like a village trusting newcomers only after many neighbours vouch, not one introducer.
